messages:
Connor O'Brien: trying to lock timing for when perf gates become blocking in CI for runtime PRs + release candidates. we need to communicate to release train + avoid surprise red builds.

Connor O'Brien: current state (as of today): `perf-smoke` job is non-blocking + posts artifacts. proposal is phased rollout: warn-only -> soft fail -> hard fail. @Sahana Iyer can you sanity check what’s feasible w/ perf-canary + CI plumbing?

Sahana Iyer: yep. perf-smoke is in the new pipeline but still marked `allow_failure` (or whatever the GH equivalent ends up being). we can flip it to required, but need a couple things first:
- stable artifact schema + upload retention (so devs can actually debug)
- clear thresholds by metric (TTFT/TPOT vs e2e) + variance allowances
- a bypass mechanism (label + approval) so we don’t deadlock emergency fixes

Mateo Alvarez: +1 on phased. we should also separate PR gating (fast + minimal shapes) vs release qualification (full baseline suite). we can’t run the whole suite on every PR.

Connor O'Brien: agree. I’m thinking:
1) PR gate: `perf-smoke` on key microbenches + 1-2 representative shapes. timebox <15 min.
2) release candidate gate: full baseline suite run (multi-region) before we cut RC.

Connor O'Brien: question: when do we make PR gate blocking? and when do we enforce RC gate?

Sahana Iyer: RC gate can be earlier because it’s “release process” not “every PR”. PR gate should stay warn-only until we trust variance budgets.

Sahana Iyer: suggested timeline:
- Phase 0 (now): warn-only PR perf-smoke, no required checks. all diffs posted to slack.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): PR perf-smoke becomes required BUT only fails on “severe regression” bucket (e.g. > X% + high confidence). else it reports but doesn’t block.
- Phase 2 (after variance study + env pinning): PR perf-smoke fully blocking per policy.

Sean Gallagher: jumping in from SRE angle: env pinning is the big one. if the runner can land on mixed driver/CUDA fleet we’ll page ourselves for noise. do we have a constraint yet?

Sahana Iyer: not fully. runner can request labels, but enforcement is still weak. Marcus mentioned a fleet “pinned pool” option.

Marcus Reed: yeah we can route perf jobs to a pinned pool for baseline + gating. that’s on the perf-canary side. still WIP but doable.

Kira Volkov: also need the exception workflow. if a PR is blocked, who approves override? I’d like something concrete (label + 2 approvals, or release eng + runtime perf).

Connor O'Brien: propose:
- override label: `perf-gate-exception`
- required approvals: Release Eng (me or Sahana) + Runtime perf architect (Noah) OR Runtime manager (Mateo) depending on severity
- must include a follow-up Linear + rollback plan if regression ships

Allison Grant: please make sure whatever we do doesn’t explode metrics cardinality. if we start slicing by too many dims in CI it’ll burn ingestion budget.

Sahana Iyer: CI gate can keep dims minimal. we’ll store full detail in artifacts (json) and only emit a summary metric.

Connor O'Brien: ok. can we align on the phases + dates? aiming to announce in #eng-runtime + #eng-announcements next week.

Sahana Iyer: assuming we get PR plumbing merged this week:
- Phase 0 through end of Feb (warn-only)
- Phase 1 starting Mar 1 (required check, only blocks “severe regressions”)
- Phase 2 TBD, depends on variance doc + pinned pool readiness (target mid/late Mar)

Mateo Alvarez: that lines up with Q1 baseline timeline. but make sure Phase 1 criteria is super conservative.

Sean Gallagher: define “severe regression” precisely pls. if it’s >10% p95 TTFT on the smoke shape w/ 3 trials and stable env, ok. otherwise: don’t block.

Kira Volkov: do we have a draft policy doc to reference? we should link it in the check output.

Connor O'Brien: perf regression policy doc is being drafted by platform standards. for now I’ll put a short “CI gate policy” snippet in the check description + link to Confluence once it exists.

Sahana Iyer: also: check output should say EXACTLY what changed:
- baseline artifact id (commit SHA / tag)
- compare artifact id
- table: metric -> delta -> threshold -> pass/fail
- link to dashboard/run logs

Connor O'Brien: great. I’ll capture this in the rollout plan email and add to release qualification checklist.

Buildkite: (system) `perf-smoke` pipeline run #1842 completed (non-blocking). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/ci/1842/summary.json

Sahana Iyer: lol perfect timing. we should make that artifact link more accessible (GH check UI).

Connor O'Brien: action items:
- Connor: write up rollout phases + dates, circulate for sign-off (Mateo/Sean/Sahana)
- Sahana: confirm required-check mechanics + exception label behavior
- Marcus: confirm pinned pool availability timeline for CI + nightly
- Kira: draft exception workflow language

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup:

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: + please loop in SRE on paging semantics once it’s blocking.

Connor O'Brien: will do. closing the loop here once doc is out.
